record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: Is there an achievable Cantorval E whose boundary has Hausdorff dimension exactly 1? Is there one whose boundary has Hausdorff dimension exactly 0?

evidence.quote: Is there an achievable Cantorval E such that (i) dimH(Fr E) = 1? (ii) dimH(Fr E) = 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ of positive real numbers with $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n < \infty$, define its achievement set (set of subsums) by
$$E(a_n) = \Big\{\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n a_n : \varepsilon_n \in \{0,1\}\Big\} \subset \mathbb{R}.$$
A subset $C \subset \mathbb{R}$ is called a Cantorval (or M-Cantorval) if $C$ is a non-empty compact set such that:
(i) $C$ is the closure of its interior;
(ii) both endpoints of every nontrivial component of $C$ are accumulation points of trivial (one-point) components of $C$.
A Cantorval $C$ is called achievable if there exists a positive summable sequence $(a_n)$ with $E(a_n) = C$. Let $\operatorname{Fr} C$ denote the topological boundary of $C$ in $\mathbb{R}$, and let $\dim_H$ denote Hausdorff dimension.

Determine whether either of the following holds:
(a) There exists an achievable Cantorval $E$ with $\dim_H(\operatorname{Fr} E) = 1$.
(b) There exists an achievable Cantorval $E$ with $\dim_H(\operatorname{Fr} E) = 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on achievement sets. Related work studies fractal properties of the Guthrie–Nymann Cantorval and shows that for certain parameterized families the Hausdorff dimension of the boundary can be made to approach 0, but no explicit achievable Cantorval realizing boundary Hausdorff dimension exactly 0 or exactly 1 appears to be established in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Fractal analysis of Guthrie–Nymann's set and its generalisations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the boundary of Guthrie–Nymann-type Cantorvals; the Hausdorff dimension of the boundary approaches 0 as a parameter m → ∞, but neither value 0 nor 1 is shown to be attained by an achievable Cantorval.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work computes/bounds Hausdorff dimensions of boundaries of certain achievable Cantorvals but does not resolve whether the extreme values 0 or 1 can occur.
